artifacts.summary: Investigates claude-refresh.sh's existing snapshot/self-exclusion architecture and bounded-build-waiter.md's canonical idiom; recommends a fifth in-script pass with two candidacy families (PID-checkable canonical idiom vs. age-only legacy/name-match shapes), names the pgid-widening self-exclusion cost, decides an age-threshold-only gate independent of --force, and states hourly-cadence report-only reachability.

memory_candidates.content: claude-refresh.sh's is_live_inhibitor_target() extracts a target PID from a candidate's own argv via regex and checks kill -0 on it -- this is the reusable pattern for any future reaper pass that needs to verify liveness of a PID embedded in another process's command line (e.g. the bounded-build-waiter canonical idiom's trailing "$pid" argument), as opposed to matching on process name/argv substrings which risks self-match.

In this repo's claude-refresh.sh, SNAPSHOT_PS_FIELDS is a fixed-position field list parsed via `read a b c ... <<< line` where the last variable slurps the remainder (args). Adding any new column requires inserting it immediately before args and updating every read call site plus the large test-claude-refresh-matcher.sh fixture file (~1046 lines of synthetic ps rows at a fixed column count) -- this is a non-trivial, cross-cutting cost, not a one-line change.

Age+idle-CPU alone is not a safe reap gate for any process that legitimately polls a long-running task at 0% CPU (e.g. a bounded-build-waiter's kill -0 loop watching a multi-hour lake build) -- a live, correctly-behaving waiter looks identical to an orphaned one under that test. Precise liveness checks (kill -0 on an embedded PID) should be preferred wherever the candidate's argv makes one extractable; age+idle should be reserved for shapes where no such PID exists, or used only as a secondary/backstop floor.
